description: One substance filed as two rows whose daily ceilings DISAGREE under numeric and lexicographic comparison — 2000 for the unqualified row and 500 for the suspension. That disagreement is the entire point of this file and is why it exists beside drug-reference-substance-dosing-ceilings.json rather than inside it: every multi-row pair in that file (3000/2000, 300/150, 4000/300, 4000/2000, 50/25, 60/30, 100/200) sorts identically either way, so a sort of the ceiling SPELLINGS passes every case built on it while a sort of the NUMBERS is what production has to do. Here `"2000"` sorts before `"500"` as text and 500 before 2000 as a number, so the two orders are distinguishable in one assertion. It matters because DosingCeilingFidelityCheck reads position 0 as the strictest and returns as soon as the answer states it: with the list reversed, an answer quoting the LAXER ceiling finds it at position 0, the walk goes silent, and the check stops seeing exactly the defect issue #276 reports — with nothing else in the suite going red. The two rows publish the same mg/kg band so that the ceiling is the only thing that differs between them, and neither carries an ATC code, so no relevance gate can inject the second row for a reason other than the question naming the substance. Both bands span 0-120 so a patient's age never silences one of them. This file is not a substitute for that one: nothing here has a route qualification worth attributing, a contraindication rule, a single-row control or a shared display name, and every case about those belongs there.
